mcat_description.short: Container Conversion Service covers the bespoke modification of ISO shipping containers (typically 20ft or 40ft) into functional spaces such as site offices, portable cabins, retail units, cafés, storage rooms, and residential units, delivered as a turnkey fabrication and fitout service.
mcat_description.long: Container Conversion Service is a B2B fabrication and fitout service in which standard ISO steel shipping containers are structurally modified and internally fitted out to serve as functional built spaces. Conversions typically involve cutting openings for doors and windows, reinforcing the steel structure, adding insulation, electrical wiring, HVAC, plumbing, and interior finishing to produce ready-to-use units. The dominant commercial application in India is the site office or portable cabin for construction, infrastructure, and industrial projects, though conversions for retail pop-ups, cold storage, food service, and modular housing are also active segments. Buyers procure these as turnkey services — specifying container size, conversion type, and fitout level — with the converted unit delivered and installed at site.

market_context: Container Conversion Service is a globally active and growing B2B fabrication segment — the Shipping Container Modification Market was valued at USD 13.02 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 16.93 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 4.32% (single source — ResearchAndMarkets via Craftsmen Industries). In India, the dominant commercial application is the site office or portable cabin for construction and infrastructure projects, with sellers concentrated in Mumbai/Thane, Coimbatore, and Kochi/Ernakulam. Standard base containers are 20ft and 40ft ISO dry containers; high-cube variants (9ft 6in height) are preferred for habitable conversions due to greater internal headroom. Conversion scope ranges from basic shell modifications (door/window openings, repaint) to fully fitted units with insulation, electrical wiring, HVAC, plumbing, and interior finishing. The service is quoted per container with pricing driven by container size, condition (new/one-trip vs used), and fitout complexity. Key buyer vocabulary in India includes 'modified container', 'container cabin', 'container site office', and 'portable cabin'; sellers also use 'customised container' and 'modular container office'. No BIS or IS standard governs container conversions in India — structural integrity is governed by the base ISO container standard (ISO 668 for dimensions, ISO 1496 for testing), and electrical fitouts follow standard Indian electrical codes.
